scenes.title: ROW_NUMBER()
scenes.narration: ROW_NUMBER assigns a unique sequential integer to every row within a partition, making it the go-to tool for deduplication and pagination.

scenes.title: Key Behaviors
bullets: Returns a unique integer starting at 1 per partition
The order is set by the ORDER BY inside OVER
Ties are broken arbitrarily — no two rows share a number
Numbering restarts for each new partition
scenes.narration: ROW_NUMBER returns a unique integer that starts at one for each partition. The sequence follows the ORDER BY clause you place inside OVER. Unlike ranking functions it never gives two rows the same number, so ties are broken arbitrarily. When a new partition begins the count resets back to one.

scenes.title: Numbering Sales Within Each Region
scenes.code:
SELECT
  region,
  salesperson,
  amount,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY region
    ORDER BY amount DESC
  ) AS rn
FROM sales;
scenes.narration: In this query we partition by region and order by amount descending. ROW_NUMBER then labels the top seller in each region as one, the next as two, and so on. Because numbering restarts per region, every region has its own independent sequence. The salesperson with the highest amount always receives row number one within their region.

scenes.title: Deduplication Pattern
steps: Partition by the columns that define a duplicate
Order by a tiebreaker like most recent timestamp
Keep only the rows where the number equals 1
scenes.narration: A classic use of ROW_NUMBER is removing duplicates. You partition by the columns that identify a duplicate and order by a tiebreaker such as the latest timestamp. Each duplicate then gets a number, and you keep only the rows numbered one, which discards the older copies.

scenes.title: Keeping One Row Per Customer
scenes.code:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    email,
    updated_at,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id
      ORDER BY updated_at DESC
    ) AS rn
  FROM customer_records
)
SELECT customer_id, email, updated_at
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1;
scenes.narration: Here we wrap ROW_NUMBER in a common table expression. Inside, we partition by customer_id and order by updated_at descending so the newest record gets number one. In the outer query we filter for rn equals one, which keeps exactly the most recent record per customer and drops the stale duplicates. This is the standard, reliable deduplication idiom in SQL.

scenes.text: ROW_NUMBER() shines for deduplication (keep 1 per group) and for stable pagination when combined with an OFFSET or a BETWEEN filter on the row number.
scenes.narration: Reach for ROW_NUMBER whenever you need to keep exactly one row per group or paginate results in a deterministic order.
